title: Research: prove a sharp C5 recursive-moment floor
body:
## Summary

```text
named physical C5 (13,23,35,16,34), arbitrary finite asymmetric scalar factors
  cost20, >=6 positive terms -> product r^r <= 640000000000 < 4^20
  five terms                -> credited rank-four classification
  cost>=21                  -> exact ambient-rank comparison
  0<=a<=1/20                -> sum r^(1-a) >= 5*4^(1-a), attained
```

Add `research/c5-recursive-moment-floor/` with the proof, physical source pins, exact receipt and two separate reconstructions. This sharp local recursive-moment floor is stronger than the predecessor scalar rank-mass floor. For a>0, equality requires five positive-cost rank-four terms. It does not claim that every cost20 histogram is identical; the complete six-term split control has ranks `2,2,4,4,4,4`.

Only this already-covered core is addressed. All five residual cores and the other seventeen covered cores from PR3268 are excluded. No native program, full physical bill, supplier admission, global decoder floor, selected-frontier update or new kappa is claimed. Stop after this scoped result.

## Evidence

- **Before:** PR3256/3268's cost20 floor leaves open whether larger-rank terms improve the recursive moment. PR3248 handles only the minimum five-term boundary.
  **After:** [PROOF.md](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e7ff9dbb57da4ec88742456c6c8f422bb8a0a969/research/c5-recursive-moment-floor/PROOF.md) combines a new exact rank-product bound, Jensen's inequality and `9*20^20 < 4*21^20` to cover every finite term count throughout the stated saving interval.
- Registered CPython 3.12.15 replay passes. Both implementations agree on all 1,024 physical tariffs and 60 exact slack cases. Six optimized groups check trace omission, the necessary scalar term-count premise, a complete six-term fit, undercharging, interval seams and source/provenance corruption. Ruff and formatting pass.
- All 12 committed package/input files match `e7ff9dbb57da4ec88742456c6c8f422bb8a0a969`. A read-only Git-free export passes all three direct scripts under optimized CPython 3.13.5 and preserves every file byte. Both live inputs are canonical-main blobs. Fresh replay needs no unrelated pending-PR Git objects.
- Written arguments and separately implemented checks are not independent human or proof-kernel review. Full selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, physical/native/precision/consumer admission and hosted CI are separate obligations. Hosted checks will be monitored on this exact head.

```sh
python3.12 -I -Werror -B scripts/research_package.py \
  --package research/c5-recursive-moment-floor
```

Base and refreshed canonical main `463113d675af7410ac91d53a4fed51ec6494eb9a`, priority revision6. TASK.json records the changed `complex-rank-shape-decoder` scope, explicit overlap correction and Open next questions. Final metadata search covered 322 open PRs and 2,115 Discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings. It does not cover every diff or unpublished work.

Credit thakrarsagar/PR3256 and PR3268 for the weighted-rank/trace cost20 method; Nick Petalas/PR3248 for the five-term classification and split boundary; Tekalign/PR2782 for physical inputs and tariffs; Arham Tahir/PR2879, Sagar Thakrar/PR2484, Cinna Davis/PR1825, Adam Gall/PR1889, ctoth, Philippe Van Velzen and the retained E8/P112 geometry lineage. Existing results are reproduced or reproved, not claimed as new. The predecessor investigation is [Discussion1587](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1587#discussioncomment-19003538). No Discussion message was posted under this session's communication restriction.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** research

One isolated opt-in package. Frozen sources, shared verification tools and the selected result are unchanged. A merged archive would not by itself constitute scientific approval or supplier admission.
